item.title: SPC MD 2348
item.description:
MD 2348 CONCERNING SEVERE POTENTIAL...TORNADO WATCH LIKELY FOR PORTIONS OF SOUTHEAST ALABAMA...THE FLORIDA 

Mesoscale Discussion 2348
NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
1022 AM CDT Fri Oct 09 2026

Areas affected...portions of southeast Alabama...the Florida
Panhandle and southwest Georgia

Concerning...Severe potential...Tornado Watch likely 

Valid 091522Z - 091745Z

Probability of Watch Issuance...95 percent

SUMMARY...The tropical cyclone tornado risk will increase across the
Florida Panhandle over the next few hours. With time, this risk will
spread north/northeast into parts of southeast Alabama and southwest
Georgia through evening. A tornado watch will be issued in the
17-18z time frame.

DISCUSSION...Northeasterly low-level winds are still present across
the region in the vicinity of a stationary front draped across
northern FL and the north-central Gulf Coast ahead of Hurricane
Isaias. This boundary will lift northward across north FL and the
Panhandle as the hurricane progresses toward the coast this
afternoon. As this occurs, richer boundary layer moisture (mid to
upper 70s F dewpoints) will overspread the coastal vicinity.
Likewise, low-level winds will become more east/southeasterly as
they also continue to increase in magnitude. This will result in
enlarged, favorably curved low-level hodographs and increasing 0-1
km SRH favorable for low-level rotation. As richer boundary layer
moisture arrives, 0-3 km MLCAPE will also increase, supporting
stronger updrafts and vertical motion within supercell storms
contained in outer rain bands moving across the FL Peninsula. This
trend has already been noted within a stronger rain band over the
offshore waters to the south of the FL Panhandle and Big Bend
vicinity.

The tornado risk will increase across the FL Panhandle by early to
mid afternoon, with the risk gradually spreading northward toward
southeast AL/southwest GA this evening.

..Leitman/Smith.. 10/09/2026

item.title: SPC MD 2334
item.description:
MD 2334 CONCERNING SEVERE POTENTIAL...WATCH UNLIKELY FOR PORTIONS OF SOUTHEASTERN ARIZONA 

Mesoscale Discussion 2334
NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
0326 PM CDT Tue Sep 29 2026

Areas affected...portions of southeastern Arizona

Concerning...Severe potential...Watch unlikely 

Valid 292026Z - 292200Z

Probability of Watch Issuance...5 percent

SUMMARY...A severe gust or brief tornado may occur with one of the
stronger storms this afternoon. The severe threat should remain
sparse, with a WW issuance not anticipated.

DISCUSSION...Clearing skies and boundary-layer heating/mixing ahead
of a confluence zone, accompanying an approaching inverted surface
trough, will support continued gradual convective intensification
through the day. MRMS mosaic radar imagery has shown strengthening
storms over eastern Pima to eastern Cochise counties over the past
hours. With surface temperatures reaching 70+ F in spots, amid low
60s F dewpoints, additional storm development is likely ahead of a
developing 500 mb low over southeastern AZ. Buoyancy exceeds 500
J/kg MLCAPE over this region, along with 40+ kts of effective bulk
shear. Any of the stronger storms that can root into the boundary
layer may become surface based and spawn either a brief tornado or
severe gust. Given the expected isolated nature of the severe
threat. A WW issuance is not expected.

..Squitieri/Mosier.. 09/29/2026
